messages:
customer_ops_acme: Hey team — starting ~2025-03-12T03:12Z we're seeing ~20% of requests return 429s. No deploys on our side. URL: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate. Logs show x-ratelimit-remaining: 0. Can someone help triage?

ingrid_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a short sample request pattern? Are these streaming requests or unary?

customer_ops_acme: Mostly short unary calls from a fleet of worker pods, ~6k req/min across 120 pods. Not streaming. We saw a couple of spikes where minute rates jumped to ~9k for 30s.

samir_oncall: rate-limit-bot flagged an alert for this tenant at 03:12:10. Raising here. Do you have API keys per pod or shared?

customer_ops_acme: Shared key. Each pod fires roughly 50 req/s when processing a batch.

rate-limit-bot: ALERT: tenant acme-corp exceeded RPM threshold at 2025-03-12T03:12:10. Policy: shared-key minute cap=6000 RPM. Current observed peak=9120 RPM.

mika_eng: That matches the 429s. Shared API key means calls aggregate into one rate bucket. Two avenues: (1) client-side smoothing (token-bucket with jitter/backoff) or (2) request folding / distribute keys.

ingrid_support: Quick repro checklist: 1) capture exact X-Request-ID and timestamps for a sample 429 response; 2) paste response headers from a 429 (x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-reset, x-request-id); 3) confirm whether retries use exponential backoff + jitter.

customer_ops_acme: Attached one header snippet: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 6000
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 16
x-request-id: rwd-9a3b`

mika_eng: Good. That reset header shows we hit the minute window. Because reset was 16s, the client should back off. Do you have retries that spike at minute boundary? e.g., cron-like jobs aligning to same second?

customer_ops_acme: We do have a scheduled flush that runs every full minute per pod — that might be coordinating.

samir_oncall: That explains it — synchronized minute-boundary flushes cause short bursts that exceed RPM even if average is under. Mitigations: add small random jitter to flush timing (0-5s), implement a client-side token bucket with capacity ~= RPS target, and add linear/exponential retry with random jitter.

ingrid_support: Short-term option: we can lift the tenant rate cap temporarily while you implement smoothing — but that requires an ops change and authorization. Would you like a temporary bump to 9k RPM for 30 minutes?

customer_ops_acme: Yes please. We’ll push jitter and backoff in the next 25 minutes. Can we get a 30-minute bump?

mika_eng: I'll coordinate. From product side: note that Dedicated or per-pod API keys would avoid aggregation into a single bucket. If this pattern is expected long-term, consider Dedicated capacity or per-worker keys.

samir_oncall: Action items: 1) ingrid to request temporary RPM bump to 9k for tenant acme-corp for 30m; 2) customer to roll jittered flush and token-bucket within 25m; 3) mika to follow up on longer-term options (Dedicated / per-key guidance).

ingrid_support: @samir_oncall I submitted the support ticket to ops (REQ-20250312-01) to increase minute cap for acme-corp to 9000 for 30m. Tagging ops for approval.

rate-limit-bot: NOTE: temporary quota changes may increase cost. Monitor token-level metrics in Console -> Usage.

customer_ops_acme: Thanks, made a quick deploy with randomized flush (0-4s jitter) and added a 50ms token-bucket limiter per pod. We'll monitor and report back in ~10m.

mika_eng: One extra pointer — if many pods share a key and you can’t distribute keys, consider implementing client-side smoothing plus exponential backoff capped at ~2s to avoid retry storms at reset boundaries. Also streaming vs unary: streaming keeps long-lived connections and can reduce per-request overhead for high-fanout workloads.

customer_ops_acme: After deploy we're down to <1% 429s during a short replay. Looks much better. Appreciate the quick help.

samir_oncall: Great. Follow-up: if you expect sustained >6k RPM, let's talk Dedicated or per-key partitions. I'll schedule a solutions sync. Closing this incident once ops confirms bump removal at expiry. :white_check_mark:
summary: Customer acme-corp hit minute-bucket RPM limit due to synchronized flushes; temporary RPM bump requested; recommended client jitter, token-bucket limiter, and longer-term Dedicated/per-key guidance.
